diagnosis.summary: The 2026-10-01 orders export re-sent the entire 09-30 file (461 stale rows, order_ids 12941-13401) along with the 440 new orders, giving 901 rows. The stale keys duplicate the 09-30 partition and fail unique_stg_orders_order_id. The failure then cascades to the marts, so fct_orders and dim_customers checks are skipped. The proposed fix is to request upstream redelivery of orders for 10-01.

root_cause.explanation: The 10-01 orders landing file has a clean schema but includes the full 09-30 file re-sent (about 461 rows; the last row, order 13401, is identical in both files) plus about 440 new orders. Staging does no dedupe, so the duplicate keys fail unique_stg_orders_order_id and assert_order_totals_match_items (461 rows each). The downstream mart tests were skipped and fct_orders has no 10-01 rows. No dbt models changed and the ingest config is empty. The per-row overlap was inferred from file boundaries and counts, not checked row by row.

evidence.claim: The failing checks are the unique and totals tests on stg_orders (461 failing rows each). The mart tests were skipped, and fct_orders has 0 rows for 10-01.
raw.orders has 901 rows against a trailing median of 461. order_items and payments are in their normal ranges.
The 10-01 file ends with 09-30 order 13401, identical to the last row of the 09-30 file. This fits a re-send of the whole 09-30 file (461 + 440 = 901). The file schema is clean.
No dbt model changed, and the ingest config is empty, so this is not a bad model deploy or a schema change.
The runbook says stale rows re-sent from a previous day need redelivery, and dedupe-on-ingest is the wrong fix for that case.

alternatives_considered: deduplicate_on_ingest on order_id: the runbook says this is wrong for stale rows from another day, and it would also persist for all future loads
revert_model_change: no models differ from the deployed version
apply_column_mapping / ignore_extra_columns / set_column_parser: the schema is clean with no renamed, added or reformatted columns
rerun_only: the landing file itself is bad, so a rerun would fail the same way
escalate_to_owner (upstream_app_team): kept as the fallback if redelivery returns the same duplicates

proposal.rationale: The 2026-10-01 orders file re-sent the whole 09-30 file (order_ids 12941-13401, 461 rows) alongside the 440 new orders. Those stale rows collide with the existing 09-30 partition, which is why unique_stg_orders_order_id fails with 461 rows. The schema is clean and no models changed. The duplicate-keys runbook says dedupe-on-ingest is wrong for stale rows re-sent from a previous day and tells us to request redelivery. order_items and payments counts look normal and their checks pass, so only orders needs re-export.
